nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of MAX-SAT instances, to an instance $(n, \varphi, K)$ that is well formed (every literal of $\varphi$ has variable index less than $n$) and feasible (some assignment of truth values to the $n$ variables satisfies at least $K$ of the clauses of $\varphi$, counted with multiplicity).…
nodes.title: MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A MAX-SAT instance $(n, \varphi, K)$ is feasible when there are truth values $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ such that at least $K$ of the clauses in the list $\varphi$, counted with multiplicity, are satisfied by the assignment $v$ with $v(x) = a_x$ for $x < n$ and $v(x) = \mathrm{false}$ for $x \ge n$.
nodes.title: Feasible MAX-SAT instances

nodes.summary: A MAX-SAT instance is a triple $(n, \varphi, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of variables), a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: MAX-SAT instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY over bitstrings lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A MAX-SAT instance $(n, \varphi, K)$ is well formed when every literal $(x, b)$ in every clause of $\varphi$ has variable index $x < n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed MAX-SAT instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
